item.description:
**Download:** [Leise-2.2.3.zip](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise/releases/download/v2.2.3/Leise-2.2.3.zip) — quit Leise, then replace the old `Leise.app` in your Applications folder. (First launch after replacing: System Settings → Privacy & Security → "Open Anyway", same as before — [README](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise#readme).)
## What changed in 2.2.3
- **Spoken version numbers survive the pause.** Say 二点、二点三 or 二点.二点三 — take your clause pause wherever you like — and the digits `2.2.3` land as one number instead of `二点、2.3`. The streaming cut no longer splits a number at its spoken dot, in any of the three renderings the recogniser produces (ASCII dot, enumeration comma, or plain run-on). - **Check for updates from the main window.** A new row at the bottom of the sidebar — above the gear row, which now says "Settings" — runs one check on click, with a "You're up to date" answer right where you clicked. Never-asked machines get the consent question first; a standing "no" stays a no. - **The update prompt speaks your language, and never interrupts.** The prompt and its buttons follow the app's language (English, Deutsch, 简體/繁體中文) instead of the framework's English-only alert — and while a dictation is running, no update window appears at all: it waits until you stop talking, then presents itself. - **Translations you never asked for are caught more often.** The polish guard gained a second, smarter alignment pass: a Latin word quietly replaced by a Chinese phrase — `disclaimer` → 免责声明 was the live case — is now detected and your original wording stands, in shapes that previously sailed through (measured against the full stored history: detections up by a third, zero new false alarms on the deliberate number conversions). - **Fields that resist edits no longer accumulate duplicates.** When a correction cannot be pasted over its target (some Chromium/Electron-app fields eat the selection), Leise now writes the corrected text through the field's whole-value channel instead of leaving the sentence duplicated — and if even that fails, the failure is loud in the log instead of silent. - **Vanished dictations leave a trace.** Recording start, an empty capture, and every history filing now log one line each — the "I spoke a whole paragraph and nothing happened" report is diagnosable in minutes instead of a forensic puzzle. - **The update feed is machine-verified.** Version, byte size, download URL and signature are asserted against the uploaded file before the feed can serve it — the failure mode where a stale manifest reached users is closed.
- **The window is the content.** The title bar is gone — "Leise" now lives at the sidebar's top next to the traffic lights, and every page starts right at the top of the window instead of below a name strip. Sidebar rows (and the gear row, and the check-for-updates link) share one geometry: full-width click targets, a pointing-hand cursor on hover, and identical highlight fills — wherever the hand shows, a click works. - **"Time saved" leads the stats.** The first card on Home is now the hours typing spared you — and the math learned languages: Chinese text is costed at 30 characters a minute and English/German at 40 words a minute (researched baselines), so a Chinese-heavy workload finally shows the savings it actually earns.
## The essentials (unchanged)
**Apple Silicon only** (M1 or newer) · **macOS 14.4+** · about **7 GB free disk** (523 MB app + 5.9 GB speech models downloaded on first run).
A 100 % local dictation app for macOS. Your audio and your transcripts never leave your Mac; it works with the network off.
**macOS will refuse to open it once.** Leise is signed but not notarised. ⛔ **In both dialogs the blue default button is "Move to Trash"** — pressing Return deletes the app you just downloaded. Click **Done**, then go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, find the line about Leise, and click **Open Anyway**. Full walkthrough in English, Deutsch and 简体中文: [README](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise#readme).
**What it sends over the network.** Nothing about you. The speech models on first run, and — only if you enable update checks, which ships off — a version-number request to the update feed. Both under your control.
Coming from 2.2.2: everything above, plus the reliability work — the history writer and the capture layer now log loudly, and the update feed generator verifies itself.
Anything wrong: **Settings → General → Diagnostics → Export Diagnostics** writes a file to your Downloads folder. Send it over.
